clues: This is a town in the northwest part of Alberta, in Canada. It sits on the banks of a big stream, far northwest of Edmonton.
Pacific winds drop their rain on far hills first, so the air here stays dry. Cold Arctic air flows in with no block, and fog often fills the low land.
Long ago, it was just a small village crossing place. It stayed a village with that crossing name only from 1914 to 1916.
A creek once ran in the open through its streets. Now it runs hidden in a pipe under the roads and pops out at a park.
This town was home to the Winter Games of its province in 2004. Years later, it helped host the Summer Games too.
